payload.name: Preference extraction from enjoyment statements
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states they love, enjoy, or are a big fan of an item or category, extract a `preference` memory capturing what they enjoy, and keep any recommendation in a separate `event` memory.
content: When a message contains an explicit positive affect statement ('I love', 'I enjoy', 'I am a big fan of') about an item or category, extract a `preference` memory for the speaker that states what they enjoy (e.g., enjoying books with adventures and magic), even if the same message also contains a recommendation.
Keep the recommendation, if present, in a separate `event` memory; do not let the event memory replace or absorb the preference statement.
Generalize to the category the speaker enjoys when the loved item exemplifies it (e.g., a book series with adventures and magic means the speaker enjoys those book genres).
Do not apply to messages lacking a stated affect (pure recommendations or actions) or to non-durable one-off states about a specific item.

solves: Construction agents lose explicit enjoyment when they store a statement like 'I love this series - it has adventures and magic' as only a recommendation event, so later questions about what the speaker enjoys cannot be answered. This Skill applies when a speaker explicitly states love/enjoyment of an item or category; extract a durable `preference` memory capturing that enjoyment and keep any recommendation as a separate `event`. It must not apply to messages that only describe actions (e.g., recommending) without an affect statement, or to one-off states about a single item.
